news.title: BAPN players and coaches shine at the NZ Masters National Championships
news.excerpt: Coach Alfred Wong led the way with three national titles, with Mitch Hejl and Catherine Nguyen also winning gold and head coach Cici Xie reaching a final.
body: BAPN players and coaches came home from the NZ Masters National Championships 2026 with a haul of titles — a proud moment for the whole academy.

BAPN coach Alfred Wong led the way with three titles: Men's Singles 50+, Men's Doubles 40+ and Men's Doubles 45+. Winning in both singles and doubles across more than one age group at a national event is a remarkable achievement.
Mitch Hejl won the Women's Singles 55+ title, and Catherine Nguyen won the Division 2 Mixed Doubles. BAPN head coach Cici Xie reached the final of the Women's Doubles 35+.
Ann Lee, Anna Ritche and Slava Sirotov also represented BAPN at the championships, and every one of them did the academy proud.
The results show that at BAPN, badminton isn't just for juniors. Adult players train with the same structure and high standards — and it shows when it counts.

news.title: Elsa and Rohan dominate the 2026 Otago U17 Championships
news.excerpt: Two BAPN juniors finished on the podium in every event they entered — two titles for Elsa, a title and a third for Rohan, and silver together in the mixed.
body: BAPN juniors Elsa Meng and Rohan Gala had an outstanding weekend at the 2026 Otago U17 Championships, finishing on the podium in every event they entered.
Elsa won both the Girls' Singles and the Girls' Doubles. Rohan won the Boys' Doubles and took third place in the Boys' Singles. The pair also teamed up in the Mixed Doubles and finished second.

Results like these come from hours of work on court, and both players have earned every one of them. To celebrate, BAPN's retail partner My Badminton Shop gave Elsa and Rohan each a gift to mark their success.

news.title: BAPN juniors step onto the national pathway
news.excerpt: Marco Sun and Katrina Huang selected for the Badminton New Zealand U15 Development Squad, and Ray Gao invited to the U15 National Camp.
body: Three BAPN juniors have been recognised at national level this year.

Marco Sun and Katrina Huang were selected for the 2026 Badminton New Zealand U15 Development Squad. The squad brings together young players from across the country who show the skill, work ethic and potential to go further in the sport.

Ray Gao was invited to the 2026 U15 National Camp after a strong 2025 season, which included a Top 8 finish in Division 1 at the AIMS Games, one of the country's biggest intermediate-age sporting events.
This is exactly what BAPN's development pathway is built for: strong foundations first, then the support to take the next step when a player is ready. Congratulations, Marco, Katrina and Ray!

news.title: Rangi Ruru takes gold at the South Island Secondary Schools Championships
news.excerpt: With weekly coaching and tournament support from BAPN, Rangi Ruru's team won back-to-back gold.
body: BAPN is proud to be the coaching partner of Rangi Ruru Girls' High School's badminton programme, and the partnership has already paid off.

With weekly coaching and tournament support from BAPN, Rangi Ruru's team won back-to-back gold at the South Island Secondary Schools Championships. It was a great result for the players and their school, and a reminder of how much school badminton can grow with the right support.
BAPN is committed to giving back to the community and helping grow the sport in Canterbury schools, and we look forward to seeing Rangi Ruru go even further.
